letter.opening: Your Machine Learning internship asks for a solid grasp of modern deep learning and computer vision, written as production-ready Python under version control. I co-authored a peer-reviewed paper on precisely that combination, and its numbers are why I am writing.
letter.profile_intro: I am four months into an MSc in Data Science at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, after a BTech in Computer Science and four applied internships in machine learning, generative AI and cloud operations. The most recent, at Elevate Labs, ended with recognition as Best Performer of the cohort. I build models with the intention of running them, a habit picked up from cloud operations on VMware infrastructure.

achievements.impact: PrisonSecure, which I co-authored in the ICISD 2025 proceedings published by Atlantis Press, reached 95.79% mAP@0.5 for weapon detection with YOLOv11 and 93.75% accuracy for face recognition through FaceNet embeddings and an SVM classifier.
trained a Convolutional Neural Network in PyTorch for American Sign Language image recognition, including the full training, validation and inference pipeline with data augmentation.
delivered 10+ production-ready models across 8 end-to-end projects at Elevate Labs, in Python and under git.

achievements.lead: Automated the search instead of hand-tuning
achievements.impact: ran a GridSearchCV hyperparameter search over a Support Vector Machine to 95%+ ROC-AUC, and built a Walmart weekly-sales forecasting model with XGBoost at 96.1% R² that cut forecast error by 18%.

letter.problems_section: The posting describes adding machine learning and computer vision capabilities to a digital microscopy platform, over data ranging from cell biology to industrial quality labs. Microscopy imagery is new to me and I would rather say so than dress it up. What transfers is the habit of asking what a false positive costs before picking a metric, which is how the weapon detection ended up relying on hard negative mining against visually similar objects. My first weeks would go into your training framework and the data itself.
letter.closing: One thing belongs on the table now. The posting is listed as full time and I am enrolled at FAU, so during the lecture period I can work up to twenty hours a week. Two arrangements work on my side: part-time at that level alongside my enrolment, or full hours inside a semester break if the duration can be aligned to one. The posting states no duration, so I may have the shape of it wrong. If neither fits how the team scoped the internship, I would rather hear it early than take up your time. My residence permit already covers student employment in Germany, I can start within two weeks, and the transcript of records is ready to send.
